doc: >

  train nothing.

  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10

      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:

        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it

        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true

    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}

      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - run: access

description:
# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,
# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay
doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}

    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - run: access

  the RDP bypass thresholds. This bias is increased when a sampler entry is
  evicted without reuse (suggesting a useless insertion in the main cache for

  sampler entry is reused (suggesting a useful insertion), making future
  bypasses less aggressive. Sampler size reduced to accommodate new state.

    kind: signed

    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design

tables:

    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}  # Original bypass logic

  - name: pc_sig

    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

    width: 6                  # Reduced width from 7 to save state (max 63 instead of 95)
    max: 63                   # INF_RD, adjusted for 6-bit width
    unset: true
  - name: predicted_reuse_confidence # New table to track confidence of reuse predictions
    scope: global

# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay_adaptive_bypass
doc: >
  Mockingjay with an adaptive bypass mechanism. A per-set bypass_confidence counter
  is added, trained by sampler outcomes. This counter dynamically adjusts the RDP
  bypass threshold to mitigate wrong_bypass and should_bypass errors observed
  across different workloads. When bypass_confidence is low (indicating past
  wrong_bypasses), the threshold is raised, making bypass less likely. When
  bypass_confidence is high (indicating successful bypasses), the threshold is
  lowered, making bypass more likely.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO
  - name: bypass_confidence   # New state for adaptive bypass
    scope: per_set
    kind: saturating
    width: 3                  # 0-7, MID is 4
    init: MID

  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {adaptive_bypass_condition: {confidence: bypass_confidence, rdp_table: rdp, rdp_index: pc_sig, base_threshold: 73, confidence_scale: 1}} # Use adaptive threshold
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache

    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it

        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true

      # If rdp was optimistic (predicted insert) but line was not reused,
      # it implies a should_bypass scenario was missed for similar lines. Increment confidence.
      - when:
          table: {table: rdp, index: signature, cmp: lte, threshold: 73} # rdp predicted insert

  params: {confidence: state, rdp_table: table, rdp_index: signature, base_threshold: {int: [0, 127]}, confidence_scale: {int: [1, 8]}}
  means: >

description:
# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,
# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay_adaptive_bypass
doc: >
  Modifies bypass decisions using a feedback table trained by sampler outcomes to adapt to
  `wrong_bypass` and `should_bypass` errors, while reducing timestamp width to fit budget.
  A new `bypass_feedback_table` tracks the effectiveness of bypass for each PC signature.
  When the sampler detects a reuse, it decrements the feedback counter for that PC,
  indicating that bypassing it would have been a `wrong_bypass`. When the sampler
  replaces an entry before reuse, it increments the feedback counter, indicating that
  inserting it was a `should_bypass`. The bypass decision for the main cache is then
  gated by this feedback: a line is only bypassed if the `bypass_feedback_table` for
  its PC signature indicates a high confidence in bypassing. To fit within the metadata
  budget, the `set_clock` and sampler `timestamp` field widths are reduced from 8 to 7 bits.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 7                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS reduced from 8 to 7 bits
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {rdp_threshold_and_feedback: {rdp_table: rdp, feedback_table: bypass_feedback_table, index: pc_sig, rdp_threshold: 73, feedback_cmp: gte, feedback_threshold: 4}}
    - {rdp_exceeds_victim_and_feedback: {rdp_table: rdp, feedback_table: bypass_feedback_table, index: pc_sig, div: 8, feedback_cmp: gte, feedback_threshold: 4}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true
  - name: bypass_feedback_table
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 3                  # 0-7, small counter
    init: MID                 # 3 for width 3

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 7, init: ZERO} # Reduced from 8 to 7 bits
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        train: {table: bypass_feedback_table, index: signature, op: decrement} # Reuse happened, so bypassing was likely wrong. Decrease bypass confidence.
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        train: {table: bypass_feedback_table, index: signature, op: decrement} # Reuse happened, so bypassing was likely wrong. Decrease bypass confidence.
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        train: {table: bypass_feedback_table, index: signature, op: increment} # Aged out, so inserting would have been useless. Increase bypass confidence.
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
      - train: {table: bypass_feedback_table, index: signature, op: increment} # Evicted before reuse, so inserting would have been useless. Increase bypass confidence.
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - run: access

    greater than rdp_threshold, AND the entry of feedback_table at the index is
    present and its value compares as feedback_cmp with feedback_threshold.

doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.

  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}

name: mockingjay_bypass_feedback
doc: >
  Mockingjay with bypass feedback. A Bypass Feedback Table (BFT) tracks the utility of bypass decisions,
  indexed by PC signature. Bypassed lines are monitored by a Bypass Watcher sampler. If a bypassed line
  is later accessed, the BFT entry for its PC signature is decremented (wrong bypass). If it is evicted
  from the watcher without being accessed, the BFT entry is incremented (correct bypass).
  The bypass decision then uses this BFT value, only bypassing if the BFT indicates a neutral or positive
  tendency for bypassing lines with that PC signature. A global clock is added for the Bypass Watcher's age.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO
  - name: global_clock
    scope: global
    kind: counter
    width: 64
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}, table: {table: bft, index: pc_sig, cmp: gte, threshold: MID}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}, table: {table: bft, index: pc_sig, cmp: gte, threshold: MID}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true
  - name: bft
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 3                  # 0-7, MID is 4
    init: MID
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

  - name: bypass_watcher
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 1}         # One global sampled set for tracking bypassed lines
    extra_index_bits: 0
    ways: 16                  # Number of entries to track recent bypassed lines
    tag_bits: 46              # Full line address tag
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 64, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: global_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true} # Evict oldest bypassed line
    on_match:
      - train: {table: bft, index: signature, op: decrement} # Wrong bypass: line was reused
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: bft, index: signature, op: increment} # Correct bypass: line was not reused
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {tick: global_clock}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - sample: bypass_watcher  # Check if this access hits a previously bypassed line
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - set: {global_clock: {add: 1}} # Increment global clock after all sampling and set aging
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - run: access
  - when: {way: NUM_WAY} # If the fill was bypassed (victim returned NUM_WAY)
    sample: bypass_watcher # Install the bypassed line's signature into the watcher

  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and

  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:

  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:

    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:

description:
name: mj_bypass_feedback
doc: >
  Adds a feedback mechanism to penalize wrong bypasses. It tracks PC signatures of bypassed
  lines using a new filter table. A subsequent miss for a tracked signature triggers a
  penalty, reducing its prediction value in the main RDP table to make future bypasses
  for that signature less likely.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:
    - predict_bypass_and_record: {predictor: rdp, filter: bypass_filter, index: pc_sig, threshold: 73}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true
  - name: bypass_filter
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 1
    init: ZERO

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache

    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}

    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO
  - name: bypassed_tracker # New state to track bypassed signatures
    scope: global
    kind: flag
    width: 1
    init: ZERO

victim:

  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative

  - name: bypass_history # New table to store PC signatures of recently bypassed lines

    on_replace:

  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.

  This version adds a feedback mechanism to correct wrong bypass decisions.
  A new `bypassed_log` sampler tracks lines that were bypassed, storing their PC signature.
  If a subsequent access to a previously bypassed line misses in the LLC,
  it signifies a wrong bypass. The original PC signature in the `rdp` table is then
  decremented to make future bypass decisions for that signature less aggressive.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true
  - name: bypass_confidence
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 2
    max: 3
    init: ZERO

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

  - name: bypassed_log
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 4} # A small number of sets to track recent bypasses
    extra_index_bits: 0
    ways: 1 # Only need to track if it was bypassed, not full shadow cache behavior
    tag_bits: 20 # Enough bits to distinguish lines
    fields:
      - {name: bypass_sig, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO} # The PC signature that caused the bypass
    victim: {key: bypass_sig, extremum: min, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true} # Simple victim choice, only one way
    on_match:
      # If we hit an entry in the bypassed_log, it means this line was previously bypassed
      # but is now being accessed again. This is a wrong bypass.
      - train: {table: rdp, index: bypass_sig, op: decrement} # Penalize the original bypass signature
      - train: {table: bypass_confidence, index: bypass_sig, op: decrement} # Decrease confidence for this signature
      - free: true # Remove it from the log, as the feedback has been applied
    install: {bypass_sig: {signature: pc_sig}} # Store the PC signature that caused the bypass

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_access: # This is where we detect a miss to a previously bypassed line
  - when: {hit: false} # Only on a miss
    sample: bypassed_log # Check if this missed line was previously bypassed

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - run: access
  - when: {bypassed: true} # If the fill was bypassed, log it
    sample: bypassed_log

    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7

tables:

    entries: 2048
    width: 1
    unset: true

  - name: sampled_cache

    extra_index_bits: 4

      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}

        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

  access:
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 7, abs: true}} # ETR max is 7
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 7}} # ETR max is 7
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_access:
  # On a miss, check if we incorrectly bypassed this line before.
  # A miss is an access where we don't have a way number yet.
  - when:
      # This is a condition that doesn't exist yet: way is NUM_WAY.
      # Let's check for the signature in bypass_log. If we get a miss on it,
      # it was a bad bypass.
      table: {table: bypass_log, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 0}
    train: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, op: decrement}
    # Consume the signal
    train: {table: bypass_log, index: pc_sig, op: decrement}


on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  # This event is also called for bypassed fills.
  # For a bypassed fill, the way number is NUM_WAY.
  # The original proposal required a way check, which doesn't exist.
  # Let's log the bypass here. The on_access rule will handle the penalty.
  # A fill that was bypassed has no way, so we can't write to per_line state.
  # However, Mockingjay bypasses *before* find_victim returns, so on_fill
  # for a bypassed line might not happen as expected.
  # Let's assume on_fill is called for a bypassed line with way == NUM_WAY.

  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}

      # Let's log the signature of any line that was predicted to be long-reuse.
      table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}
    train: {table: bypass_log, index: pc_sig, op: increment}
